summary: A fiction excerpt from a novel's Book 3 (part 172) in which the narrator, Morgan, is in a dreamlike ceremony atop a rain-soaked pyramid with Alex Goddard and Sarah. Alex transforms Morgan's appearance into a monstrous royal Maya form, invokes the "miracle of Baalum" with copal incense, and a two-headed jade-colored Vision-Serpent appears and swallows Sarah in flames. The passage ends with Morgan waking in bed, where Marcelina is standing beside her holding a candle, and she realizes the storm was real.
one_line: Morgan experiences a dreamlike Maya ceremony atop a pyramid in which Sarah is swallowed by a Vision-Serpent, then wakes in bed to Marcelina.
key_facts: Alex Goddard clasps Morgan's arm and directs her to look down at a plaza where a crowd is waiting.
Alex Goddard holds up a silver mirror and tells Morgan her nose has been built up with clay and pierced with lustrous blue feathers and a giant topaz.
Morgan's front teeth have been filed to a point and inlaid with jewels, and her skull has been shaped back and flattened.
Alex Goddard ignites balls of sticky white copal resin, bark and grasses in a waist-high censer using a fire stick spun by a bow.
Alex Goddard announces, "Now we will make a miracle, the miracle of Baalum."
Morgan and Alex perform a stiff pas de deux while the strains of a clay flute drift around them.
A faint jade-colored undulating serpent forms into a two-headed specter that pirouettes above the platform.
Sarah steps toward the two-headed specter and holds out her arms.
Morgan screams for Sarah to get back, but the thing reaches down and swallows Sarah in flames.
The narrator identifies the creature as the Vision-Serpent come to receive Sarah.
Morgan wakes in a bed to find Marcelina standing beside it, dressed in white and holding a candle.
Morgan feels the moistness of the sheets and realizes the storm was real.
